boundary: Complete fresh Node and native development-helper processes; within each sample start after the same synthetic raw body and fixed identity/header inputs are available, immediately before parse. End after validation, full real Router and real token-counter processing, required and speculative immediate-mock work, compatibility and prepared serialization have completed. Both engines use their real parser/policy/classifier/excerpt/rubric/redaction/cache machinery; neither compares a pure call with the other engine's HTTP/process timing.
workload: The exact local-benchmark-v3 large_catalog_miss fixture:300 tools,30 description repetitions, claude-opus-5-5 source, compatible profile, sonnet evaluator answer at confidence1, one speculative Haiku count with1000 tokens per miss; existing conservative guard retains the source model. Same raw serialized fixture, index bytes and independent prompt/request identities in both engines. Use one sequential client; concurrent HTTP/resource workloads remain in separate protocols.
mock_policy: Use immediate in-memory transport injection through the supported Node fetchImpl and Rust HttpTransport interfaces, retaining request construction, bounded answer parsing, classifier sharing, counters and token-cache identities. No networking/provider/model/download operation is available to either stub. Record per-endpoint call counts and ordered SHA256 of exact evaluator/count payloads. Rust's advisory count may be scheduled after Router.return; a request-call observation alone is insufficient. Node awaits each real token-counter promise, including body parse/cache/finally; Rust tracks immediate count-body EOF/abandonment before clock stop on its current-thread executor (the real counter has no async suspension after decoded EOF before parse/cache insertion/return). Require one completed count and zero abandoned replies per sample. Before any numerical result, original deterministic validation1/2 hashes remain retained but do not qualify this refined timing boundary.
verification: Verify every raw/prepared body and expected model, complete validation result, exactly one evaluator and one count call per request, endpoint payload hashes and fixture identity. Compare all decision metadata by sorted-key JS-semantic SHA256, excluding only latency_ms and evaluation_latency_ms; never normalize a model/reason/guard/confidence away. Retain each round's public synthetic input record and matching output/call/decision hashes before constructing a timing comparison. Hashing and detailed verification happen after each sample's clock stops. Simulated successful completion evidence outside timing retires the task state; it is not a provider/downstream forwarding claim.
ordering: Node then Rust on odd rounds; Rust then Node on even rounds
percentile: Nearest rank independently in each round;2000 samples include20 observations in the upper one percent
uncertainty: 5000 deterministic paired bootstrap resamples over five paired rounds, seed1597463007, median paired ratio and95% interval; no outlier removal
qualification: This is an explicit gateway body-processing component, not an instrumented shipping server or installed-artifact measurement. Missing HTTP pre/postprocessing prevents this result alone approving the whole gateway processing gate. Record exact helper/source/toolchain/binary/fixture hashes and real versus synthetic evidence separately. Controlled representative hardware and other declared workload/resource/live gates remain required.
validation: --validate uses one paired round,8 warmup and32 measured samples, retains matching input/output/call evidence and strips raw/numeric processing times. Numerical runs require a release driver and helpers built with the same pinned release profile; fresh immutable binaries/source are required before acceptance work. A child control record is capped at1MiB and a child run at30 minutes; each sample's advisory completion wait is bounded at10s. No threshold, deadline, cache key or policy changes are made.
